description: Adds a connection (arrow/edge) between two nodes or containers in a live Trident document. Use get_document_summary to get valid source and target IDs before calling this. Requires a valid editor access token. For ERD relationships, connect the two TABLE containers (field rows are rejected as endpoints) and set type to an ERD pair such as "one_to_many".

action_explanation.description: Optional: brief explanation of what this action does and why (max 250 chars). Shown live to human collaborators in the AI cursor tooltip.

agentId.description: YOUR AI assistant name (e.g. "Claude.ai", "GitHub Copilot"). Shown as "[agentId] working with [userName]" in the collaboration presence dot.

id.description: Optional: unique ID; auto-generated if omitted

label.description: Optional: label shown on the connection

routingMode.description: Optional: routing algorithm: "straight" (default), "bezier", or "orthogonal". Avoid "orthogonal" unless the user asks for it: edges on one side of a node share a single port, so right-angle paths overlap.

type.description: Optional: connection type. Line styles: "arrow" (default), "line", "thick_arrow", "dashed_arrow", "dotted_arrow", "wave" (avoid unless the user asks for it: renders as a thick ribbon that hides labels). ERD relationship pairs "<source>_to_<target>", each end one of one | many | zero_or_one | zero_or_many | one_or_many — e.g. "one_to_many", "one_to_zero_or_many", "many_to_many", "one_to_one". ERD pairs are solid lines with crow's-foot markers at each end.

token.description: Editor access token for this document. The document ID is embedded in the token.

userName.description: First name of the human you are assisting (ask them at session start if you do not know). Shown in the collaboration presence dot as "[agentId] working with [userName]".

name: add_connection
